name: duckdb
license_evidence: LICENSE in the pinned v2.0.0 release-tag archive (MIT permission notice, Copyright 2018-2026 Stichting DuckDB Foundation)
input_api: duckdb::Parser::GetBuiltinParser(); Parser::ParseQuery(local SQL text) -> Parser::statements (SQLStatement trees)
dialect: DuckDB built-in grammar (Parser::GetBuiltinParser; no client context)
scope: SQL statements from local bytes parsed by duckdb::Parser with the built-in grammar and no database or client context; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary read from the SQLStatement trees. Binding, planning, execution and extension parser hooks are untested.
family: DuckDB PEG parser (own grammar and transformer)
family_note: Parser::ParseQuery runs DuckDB's tokenizer and packrat PEG matcher over the built-in .gram grammar and its transformer, which builds SelectStatement/SelectNode, InsertStatement/InsertQueryNode, TableRef and ParsedExpression trees. The adapter walks select_list, the BaseTableRef/JoinRef FROM tree, where_clause, groups, ORDER modifiers, VALUES lists, FunctionExpression names and ConstantExpression literals. The transformer stores COUNT(*) as the zero-argument function count_star; the adapter reports it as count. DuckDB 1.x used a libpg_query-derived bison grammar (PostgreSQL grammar family); v2.0.0 no longer contains it, so this path is not counted in the PostgreSQL family. The popcon count is for the Debian duckdb source package, whose packaged release line is not recorded in the snapshot; the pinned release is the current upstream tag. The parser header is installed and commented but DuckDB documents its C++ API as internal, so this is a public-header API rather than a stability-guaranteed one.

popularity.metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations, source package duckdb
popularity.limitation: Very small count; packaged installs of the whole engine (mostly the CLI), not use of its SQL parser or of the Python/R/Node bindings.

name: googlesql
license_evidence: LICENSE in the pinned 2026.11.2 release-tag archive (Apache License, Version 2.0)
input_api: googlesql::ParseNextStatement(ParseResumeLocation over local SQL text, ParserOptions{LanguageOptions()}, &ParserOutput, &at_end_of_input) -> ParserOutput::statement() (ASTStatement tree)
dialect: GoogleSQL default grammar (ParserOptions with default LanguageOptions; no catalog, no analyzer, no macro expansion)
scope: SQL statements from local bytes parsed by googlesql::ParseNextStatement with default LanguageOptions and no catalog; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary read from the AST. Name resolution, the analyzer, the reference evaluator and dialect-specific syntax are untested.
family_note: ParseNextStatement runs GoogleSQL's tokenizer and lookahead transformer and the LALR parser that Textmapper generates from googlesql/parser/googlesql.tm at build time, which builds generated ASTNode classes. The adapter walks ASTSelect select_list, where_clause and group_by, ASTOrderBy ordering_expressions, ASTJoin nodes, ASTTablePathExpression and ASTInsertStatement target paths, the INSERT column list and ASTInsertValuesRowList rows, ASTFunctionCall names, ASTStringLiteral values and ASTIntLiteral/ASTFloatLiteral images. Own grammar, independent of the PostgreSQL (libpg_query), DuckDB PEG, libgda, SQLite and tree-sitter-sql grammars. Upstream calls googlesql/parser semi-public because parse trees are not a stable API, and the //googlesql/parser Bazel target is visible only inside //googlesql/..., so the harness is built as a package in that tree. The repository was named google/zetasql until 2026; the GitHub API resolves both names to google/googlesql.

popularity.metric: GitHub stars (secondary, repository interest, not downloads)
popularity.limitation: Star-fallback path (C and C++ rule of 2026-11-18): GoogleSQL has no Debian source or development package in the pinned popcon snapshot and no vcpkg or Conan port, so it has no primary or Debian-fallback value. Stars measure interest in the whole GoogleSQL repository (parser, analyzer, reference implementation and Java/Go front ends), not installs or use of its parser; they are ranked separately, after the popcon-ranked path, and never compared with popcon counts.
